title: An eigenembedding for a periodic simple geometric local system
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field, ℓ a different prime, and X/k₀ a scheme with irreducible geometric fiber. Let V be a lisse Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and let S be an irreducible geometric local system admitting an embedding j:S → V̄. For any d≥0 and isomorphism e:(Fr^d)^*S ≅ S, there exist a monomorphism j′:S → V̄ and an isomorphism e′:(Fr^d)^*S ≅ S satisfying e′;j′ = (Fr^d)^*(j′);φ_d. No irreducibility or semisimplicity of V is assumed.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--2: the eigenline of the multiplicity operator, expressed as an eigenvector in Hom(S,V̄).

proof.text: Give morphisms of adic sheaves their coefficient-vector-space structure using scalar endomorphisms and the faithful forgetful functor to sheaves. Pushforward is linear; its left adjoint pullback is linear too. Consequently evaluation at a geometric point is linear. A nonzero morphism out of S is mono, since its lisse kernel must be zero by simplicity. If its stalk is zero this contradicts the nonzero stalk rank of S. Thus stalk evaluation on Hom(S,V̄) is injective. Finite-dimensionality of the two lisse stalks makes Hom(S,V̄) finite dimensional; the supplied embedding makes it nonzero.

Let Q=(Fr^d)^* and define the coefficient-linear endomorphism B(f)=e^{-1};Q(f);φ_d on Hom(S,V̄). It is injective, since Q is faithful and the two outer arrows are isomorphisms. Mathlib Module.End.exists_eigenvalue and HasEigenvalue.exists_hasEigenvector supply a nonzero eigenvector v with eigenvalue c. Injectivity implies c≠0.

The nonzero eigenvector v:S→V̄ is mono by the kernel argument. Set e′ to the isomorphism with hom c•e.hom and inverse c^{-1}•e.inv. The two inverse identities follow by coefficient linearity and c≠0. Composing the eigenvector equation with e.hom gives precisely e′.hom;v=Q(v);φ_d. This also covers d=0.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1--2, adapted to the Hom space of sheaf morphisms, using the existing lisse-kernel and stalk-rank API and Mathlib eigenvalues.

mathlib_searches.query: An invertible linear operator on a nonzero finite dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field has a nonzero eigenvector with nonzero eigenvalue
mathlib_searches.results: Module.End.exists_eigenvalue; Module.End.HasEigenvalue.exists_hasEigenvector; LinearMap.not_hasEigenvalue_zero_tfae. The first two are used directly; the nonzero eigenvalue is proved from injectivity.
Exact eigenvalue-existence theorem in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Eigenspace.Triangularizable; sheaf Hom-space and Frobenius compatibility still require proof.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_simple_frobenius_eigenembedding
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [IrreducibleSpace (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber]
    (V : WeilSheaf k₀ l X) (hV : V.IsLisse)
    (S : AdicSheaf l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber)
    (hS : IsIrreducibleAdicLocalSystem S) (j : S ⟶ V.obj.carrier) [Mono j]
    (d : ℕ) (e : (ProEtaleWeilSheaf.frobeniusPowPullback k₀ l X d).obj S ≅ S) :
    ∃ (j' : S ⟶ V.obj.carrier), Mono j' ∧
      ∃ e' : (ProEtaleWeilSheaf.frobeniusPowPullback k₀ l X d).obj S ≅ S,
        e'.hom ≫ j' =
          (ProEtaleWeilSheaf.frobeniusPowPullback k₀ l X d).map j' ≫
            (V.obj.frobeniusPowIso d).hom
